config_fetch.argument: the callee's only argument is rdi, a pointer to a 0x50-byte struct the caller seeded on its own stack immediately before the call.  Both shaper seeds are pinned byte-for-byte: sentinel qwords 0x8000000000000000 at +0x0/+0x18/+0x30 (lvl4_a stores at 0x2ae4244/0x2ae424c/0x2ae4266 over base [rsp+0xd0]; lvl3_c at 0x2cde4e5/0x2cde4ed/0x2cde507 over base [rsp+0x190]), the dword 0x64 at +0x48, the sete byte ([0x64f01b0] == 2) at +0x4c and the word 0x100 at +0x4d, each preceded by the lazy-state guard (the dword load at 0x2ae4225 / 0x2cde4c6 and its init arm).  The other two callers seed the same shape (sentinels at +0x0, the 0x64 dword at +0x48, the sete byte at +0x4c; their pinned stores are in the packet as absolute site pins, with the +0x4d byte copied from their caller's [rbx+0x11d] and a 0x1 word at +0x4e).
config_fetch.body: the callee compares the struct's head qword ([rdi], 0x1506852) against 0x8000000000000001 (0x1506859).  On the equal arm it stages a default built from globals: the lazy-state dword at 0x64f01b8 (0x150685e; a nonzero value first takes the once-init arm at 0x15069b5, which calls the 0x64df9f0-slot body 0x5c87d50 with rdi = &0x64f01b8), the state byte at 0x64f01b0 compared to 2 (0x150686e, sete at 0x1506875), that flag ORed into the 16-byte .rodata constant at 0x454950 (por at 0x150687c; the constant is 00 00 01 00 followed by zeros, so the staged +0x4c byte is the flag and the +0x4d word is 0x100), the sentinel for the staged +0x0/+0x18/+0x30 and 0xa (0x1506884) for the staged +0x48 dword.  On the other arm it stages a byte copy of the caller's [rdi..rdi+0x50] (loads at 0x1506891..0x15068c0).  The three 16-byte fields of the default arm's staging (+0x8..+0x18, +0x20..+0x30, +0x38..+0x48) are read from the callee's own frame slots at [rsp+0xa0], [rsp+0x90] and [rsp+0x80], which that arm never writes; only the copy arm writes them (from the caller's struct).  Both arms converge on the store sequence at 0x15068c5, which lays the staged 0x50 bytes at [rsp+0x18].

config_fetch.question: what does the config fetch through GOT slot 0x64e0a80 return, and what do builder_c and lvl4_a's inlined build read from it beyond the "hl-node" key (phase-producer packet, open edge 1)
config_fetch.return: nothing.  A complete bracket census of the callee classifies eight loads through rdi (+0x0 at 0x1506852, then the copy arm's +0x8/+0x18/+0x20/+0x30/+0x38/+0x48/+0x4c at 0x1506891..0x15068c0) and no store through rdi, no lea of rdi, and no other-destination access: every store in the body lands in the callee's own frame ([rsp+0x18] staging and the log-arm descriptors).  The struct the caller seeded is byte-identical after the call.  No caller consumes a return value: after lvl4_a's call the next instruction (0x2ae4287) loads edi = 0x7 for the key allocation, after lvl3_c's call the next instruction (0x2cde52b) loads rdi with builder_c's record buffer, and the other two sites continue with loads from their own frames (0x2aeb2e6, 0x2cb68f6); no test of rax follows any of the four calls.
config_fetch.slot: GOT slot 0x64e0a80 carries exactly one R_X86_64_RELATIVE relocation, addend 0x1506840; the callee body is 0x1506840..0x15069f2 (434 bytes).  Its complete rip-relative reference list (series census method) is four FF 15 call sites: 0x2ae4281 in lvl4_a, 0x2aeb2e0 in the body 0x2aeaef0..0x2af0654, 0x2cb68f0 in the gate body 0x2cb6500..0x2cbbbdf, and 0x2cde525 in lvl3_c.  No instruction anywhere calls or tail-calls 0x1506840 directly (the E8/E9 census for the callee is empty), and builder_c (0x2b7b640) contains no reference to the slot at all: its rip-target map is pinned and the slot is not in it.

limits: Static trace only: no captured instruction was executed and no concrete input values were observed.  The bracket censuses classify each instruction of the censused bodies by operand position in fresh objdump text (a mov-family bracket destination is a store, a bracket source is a load, a lea bracket is an address-taken); register identity follows the entry assignments (rbx = rsi in the predicate, set once at 0x14c2a49; rbx = rdi in lookup_d, set once at 0x564ccf4; rdi in config_fetch and lookup_a is the entry argument throughout).  The config slot's binary-wide reference list uses the series census method (REX-prefixed modrm-checked forms and FF 15/FF 25 over .text); the four references it finds are each pinned byte-for-byte at instruction boundaries, and the in-body rip-target maps are read from instruction-aligned objdump text, not from the byte scan.  A whole-struct copy moves bytes without naming fields: the copies (the callee's staging, lookup_c's 0x250-byte memcpy, builder_c's 0x98-byte memcpy, lookup_d's [rsp+0x20] value copy) are enumerated as call sites with pinned argument setups, so for copied fields the census is a statement about direct accesses and the copies actually observed.  Arm attribution follows the branch structure read from the disassembly (the head-qword compares, the predicate's test, the chain field's length and byte compares); reachability beyond that structure is not re-decided here.  Strings are read through the section table (.rodata is identity-mapped in this ELF, .text resolves at VA - 0x1000 and .data.rel.ro at VA - 0x2000, all through the section headers, never by a fixed delta), and every named string is re-read on every run and fails closed on drift.  Raw values are recorded mechanically; no field types are guessed.

predicate.arms: if the global's dword at +0x40 is nonzero (0x14c2a5b) the predicate first calls 0x15d3214 with rdi = global+0x18 (0x14c2b2f).  It then calls the 0x64dffe0-slot body 0x154cd10 (0x14c2a69) with rdi = global+0x18, rsi = the global's +0x8 qword and rdx = its +0x10 qword.  If that returns nonzero, the predicate emits its own log record through slot 0x64df4b8 (0x14c2a91, rdi = 0x448a8e) and validates each of the staged copy's three {length, pointer} fields (+0x0/+0x8, +0x18/+0x20, +0x30/+0x38): for each nonzero length it calls the 0x64df4a0-slot body 0x635de30 with (pointer, length, 0) (calls at 0x14c2aa5, 0x14c2aba, 0x14c2ad1), then returns 1.  If the check returns zero, the predicate copies the staged 0x50 bytes into its own frame, appends the global pointer, and calls 0x154c2c0 (0x14c2b1d) with rdi = global+0x18, edx = 1 and rcx = 0x63f8db0; that call's result is the predicate's return value.
predicate.body: the predicate 0x14c2a40..0x14c2b4c (268 bytes) takes rdi = the global struct at 0x64efd00 and rsi = the staged copy.  It holds rsi in rbx (0x14c2a49) and rdi in r14 (0x14c2a4c).  A complete bracket census through rbx shows loads only -- the staged fields at +0x0/+0x8 (0x14c2a97, 0x14c2a9f), +0x18/+0x20 (0x14c2aab, 0x14c2ab4), +0x30/+0x38 (0x14c2ac0, 0x14c2acb) and the wholesale copy loads at +0x0..+0x40 (0x14c2ae4..0x14c2aef) and +0x40 (0x14c2adb) -- and no store through rbx: the staged copy is read, never written.

record_attribution.builder_c_sequence: builder_c never calls the config check (its rip-target map has no 0x64e0a80 entry).  It allocates the 7-byte key through slot 0x64df480 (body 0x6355830), writes the "hl-node" bytes into it from 0x92a890, and forms the key descriptor {7, pointer, 7} at [rsp+0x50].  Then, in order: lookup_a (call at 0x2b7b69b) with rdi = &[rsp+0x2a0] and rsi = the key descriptor; lookup_b (call at 0x2b7b6ac) with rdi = &[rsp+0x50] and rsi = &[rsp+0x2a0]; lookup_c (call at 0x2b7b6b8) with rdi = rsp and rsi = &[rsp+0x50].  lvl4_a runs the same three calls inlined on its dispatch arm, after the config check, with the entry at [rsp+0xd0] and the key descriptor at [rsp+0x380].
record_attribution.chain_tag: the tag byte comes from the converted value's "chain" field: lookup_d looks the 5-byte key at 0x92a7be ("chain") up through the direct callee 0x4e4ca30 (call at 0x564cd06, length at 0x564ccfe).  A 5-byte value equal to "Local" (the xor compares at 0x564cd20/0x564cd27) gives 0; a 7-byte value equal to "Sandbox" (0x564cd36) gives 1, to "Testnet" (0x564cd49) gives 2, to "Mainnet" (0x564cd5c) gives 3.  Any other value, or a missing field, takes the panic arms: the unwrap call through slot 0x64df6a0 with the 43-byte message at 0x92a732 ("called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value", call at 0x564cd91) or the panic bodies through slot 0x64df830 (calls at 0x564ceea, 0x564cef7).
record_attribution.fetch_role: the config check's only connection to the record is ordering: in the two shapers it runs on the seeded struct before lookup_a overwrites that struct as the entry, and its default arm reads the same two globals (0x64f01b0, 0x64f01b8) the shapers' seeds derive their +0x4c flag from.  It reads the seed and the globals; it writes nothing any later instruction can observe.
record_attribution.lookup_a: lookup_a (0x163a4b0..0x163a66c) returns rdi and writes the 0x250-byte default entry there.  Its complete store census through rdi (44 store sites) shows: the key descriptor is copied verbatim to entry +0x20 (movups at 0x163a4be) and +0x30 (the descriptor's third qword, at 0x163a4b7); the sentinel lands at +0x38 (0x163a4cc), +0x50 (0x163a51d) and +0x68 (0x163a52c); the head +0x0 and +0x10 are zeroed (0x163a546, 0x163a54d); +0x110 takes 0x3e7 (0x163a53b), +0x1e8 takes 0x1020700 (0x163a560), +0x248 takes 0x11000000110000 (0x163a638); nine {0, 0, 8} triples and the remaining single qwords are zeroed as the census table lists.  No store in the census covers the window [entry+0x40, entry+0x50): in lvl4_a the caller's seeded +0x48 dword (0x64), +0x4c flag byte and +0x4d word survive into the entry there, the +0x40 qword is written by neither the seed nor lookup_a, and in builder_c the whole window is the fresh frame's residue.
record_attribution.lookup_b: lookup_b (0x564d700..0x564df8c, 2188 bytes) is called with rdi = the slot that held the key descriptor and rsi = the entry; lookup_c then memcpy's 0x250 bytes from that slot, so the slot holds the entry lookup_c converts.  lookup_b's internal reads and writes are not reversed in this packet (see boundaries).
record_attribution.lookup_c: lookup_c (0x165de90..0x165dfaa) memcpy's the 0x250-byte entry from its rsi into its own frame (call at 0x165deae, length pinned at 0x165dea9), initialises a context at [rsp+0x8] through slot 0x64e1290 (call at 0x165deb9), and calls its worker 0x165dfb0 (0x165decc) with rdi = the output pointer, rsi = the entry copy and rdx = the context; the worker holds rdi in rbx and first reads the entry at +0x1e8 (lea at 0x165dfca).  lookup_c then drops the entry copy through 0x165e570 (0x165ded6) and releases the context's string vector through the 0x64df4a0 dealloc slot.  The converted value lookup_c leaves at its rdi is what builder_c tests and lookup_d queries.
record_attribution.lookup_d_arm: on the other arm builder_c copies the converted value over the key descriptor slot, calls lookup_d (0x2b7b73f) with rdi = the entry and rsi = the copy, drops the value through 0x2ab8cc0, and memcpy's the entry's first 0x98 bytes into the record (length at 0x2b7b755, call at 0x2b7b75d).  lookup_d's complete store census through its entry pointer is twelve sites: +0x0, +0x10, +0x20, +0x30, +0x40, +0x50, +0x60 and +0x70 (the copies at 0x564ceb2..0x564ce70) take the 0x78-byte value the 0x64ebcb0-slot callee 0x5654bf0 builds at lookup_d's [rsp+0x20] (call at 0x564ce57) from a descriptor {[rsp+0x8], [rsp+0x10], [rsp+0x18]} formed out of the converted value's +0x48 sub-object -- its +0x8, +0x10 and base+0x18 -- or the defaults {rdx = 1, rax = 0, rcx = 0} when that pointer is null; +0x78 (0x564cebc) and +0x88 (0x564cec7) take the "key" field's length; +0x80 (0x564cec0) takes a fresh allocation (slot 0x64df480) holding a copy of that string's bytes (memcpy at 0x564ce06); and the byte at +0x90 (0x564ceb5) takes the chain tag.  When the "key" field is absent (the lookup at 0x564cdae returns null), +0x78 and +0x88 take the sentinel 0x8000000000000000 and no instruction on that arm writes r12, so +0x80 takes the caller's r12 (in lvl4_a, the entry pointer set at 0x2ae42ea).  When the built value's head dword is 0x10 the arm takes a panic call instead (cmp at 0x564ce5d).

record_attribution.tagged_arm: builder_c compares the converted value's head qword at [rsp] against 0x8000000000000001 (movabs at 0x2b7b6be, cmp at 0x2b7b6c8).  On the equal arm it writes the record itself: record +0x0 = 0x10 (store at 0x2b7b6f2) and record +0x8..+0x40 copied from the value's +0x8..+0x40 (the movups copies at 0x2b7b6d7..0x2b7b6ee and the +0x38 qword at 0x2b7b6d3).
